title: stall-fence-and-graceful-retirement-coordinator-for-continuous-batcher
author: Lukas Meyer
description: Context: Continuous-batcher tail latency regressions were observed under mixed workloads that contain intermittent KV-heavy requests which pin large KV-cache entries. Motivation: reduce long-tail stalls without regressing overall throughput or increasing token cost. This PR introduces a "stall fence" plus a graceful retirement coordinator that: 1) detects per-lane sustained stall conditions (configurable threshold) using a lightweight sliding-window of enqueue/dequeue latencies; 2) inserts a soft retirement window for older slots so that pinned KV-heavy requests can be drained without starving incoming short-requests; 3) applies a short-term KV-pin TTL extension heuristic when retirement is happening to avoid immediate re-pinning thrash; 4) surfaces new metrics and tracing spans for the fence/retire lifecycle so operators can correlate stalls to KV pressure and kernel hints. Design highlights: - Stall fence is enforced via a lane-local watermark and a global backpressure token bucket. It only triggers when p95 enqueue latency and queue occupancy exceed configured buckets to avoid oscillation. - Graceful retirement uses a conservative aging credit: a slot is marked 'retiring' and allowed to complete, but new work is softly deprioritized in that slot; the coordinator can fast-path short sequences to other lanes if capacity exists. - KV-pin TTL heuristic: when a slot enters retirement and the kernel is about to pin large embeddings, the TTL is extended by an exponential-backoff step to reduce re-pin churn across short successive retires. - Kernel hint: scheduler now passes a "short-priority" hint for requests with sequence-length <= 64 to bias small requests to landing slots. - Feature-flagged rollout: disabled by default for Dedicated until a canary passes. Implementation notes: changes are minimal and localized to continuous_batcher scheduler, kv/pin_manager, and the runtime config. All API surfaces remain backward compatible. See the checklist below for what was added/tested. Checklist: - [x] Add stall fence and retirement coordinator logic (continuous_batcher/*) - [x] KV pin TTL heuristic and instrumentation (kv/*) - [x] Kernel hint plumbing for short-priority (runtime/kernel_hints.go) - [x] Unit tests and deterministic clock for retirement behavior - [x] Microbenchmarks (mixed kv-heavy vs short-request) - [x] Console metrics and tracing spans - [x] Feature flag and rollout plan The description above summarizes rationale, design, and the rollout approach.
commits_summary: 5 commits: initial coordinator and fence implementation; add KV-pin heuristic and kernel hint plumbing; unit tests + deterministic clock; microbench harness for mixed workload; docs + rollout flags and observability additions.
tests_and_benchmarks: Added deterministic unit tests that exercise retirement windows and fence triggers (retire_test.go). Microbenchmarks run on CI bench runner show: mixed workload (70% short seq <=64, 30% KV-heavy) p99 latency reduced by ~18% under the canary config and steady-state throughput improved ~2%. A small tradeoff: p50 unchanged, p95 improved ~10% during KV spike scenarios. Bench harness and raw artifacts attached in CI.
